title: A Life Begins
text: Before the sword, before the name, there was only where you came from.

choices.text: An orphan sleeping under the bridge

success.text: Hunger taught you to read faces before you could read words.

choices.text: A farmer's child with calloused hands

success.text: You carried water before you could run.

choices.text: A merchant's child raised on an abacus

success.text: You learned early that everything has a price.

choices.text: Last heir of a slaughtered martial clan

success.text: You remember fire, and a man with a scar across his palm. A servant carried you out.
Your cradle was a stolen saddle.

title: The Old Beggar
text: At the edge of the market, an old beggar with clear eyes holds out a strange black pill.

success.text: Warmth floods your meridians. The beggar is gone when you look up.

fail.text: Your stomach burns for three days.

success.text: He chuckles. "Caution is also a kind of talent."
It is genuine. You swallow it without fear.

choices.text: Snatch his begging bowl and run

success.text: Six copper coins. He watches you go with something like pity.

fail.text: He trips you with his cane without even looking.

title: The Bully of the Lane
text: A bigger boy has a small child pinned in the mud, stuffing dirt in his mouth.

success.text: You bloody his nose. The small child looks at you like a hero from the tales.

fail.text: He beats you both. Still, the small child shares his rice cake with you.

success.text: The bully gets the cane. Sensible, if not glorious.

choices.text: Hold the kid's legs for him

success.text: The bully grins and shares the stolen sweets with you.

title: The Steamed Bun
text: You have not eaten in two days. A bun seller turns his back to argue with a customer.

success.text: It is the best thing you have ever tasted.

fail.text: He catches your wrist and thrashes you in front of the whole street.

choices.text: Offer to wash his steamers for a bun

success.text: He grunts, then gives you two.
The hunger sharpens something in you.

title: The River Takes a Child
text: Screams by the river. A child is being swept toward the rapids.

success.text: You drag the child ashore, half drowned yourself. The mother weeps on your shoulder.

fail.text: The current smashes you on the rocks. Fishermen pull you both out.

choices.text: Run along the bank with a pole

success.text: You hook the child's collar at the last bend.

fail.text: Too slow. A fisherman downstream does what you could not.

success.text: Someone else jumps. You tell yourself there was nothing you could do.

title: The Wooden Sword
text: You whittle a sword from a branch and swing it a thousand times behind the barn.

success.text: Your palms split and heal harder.

choices.text: Imitate the swordsmen you have seen

success.text: One swing whistles. You do not know why, and chase that sound for years.

fail.text: You hit yourself in the shin.

title: The Village Teacher
text: The old scholar offers free lessons to any child who can sit still.

success.text: One day you will read manuals that others can only stare at.

choices.text: Skip class to race along the rooftops

success.text: The tiles are loose and your feet learn to be light.

choices.text: Steal his inkstone and sell it

success.text: A fine inkstone, it turns out.

title: Lantern Festival
text: In the festival crowd you see a thin hand lift a purse from a merchant's belt.

success.text: The merchant rewards you and tells everyone your name.

fail.text: The thief's knife opens your forearm before he vanishes.

choices.text: Follow him and demand a share

success.text: He laughs and teaches you the two-finger lift for half the purse.

fail.text: His gang is waiting in the alley.

success.text: The lights float up like souls. Not your purse, not your problem.

title: The Missing Chickens
text: A neighbour's chickens are gone and he is pointing at you. You know the cook's son did it.

success.text: Feathers in the cook's yard. The neighbour apologises with eggs.

fail.text: Nobody believes you. You get the switch.

success.text: The cook's son watches, pale. That night he leaves his best marble on your windowsill.

choices.text: Blame the crippled beggar boy instead

success.text: It works. They drive him out of the village.

title: The Boar in the Millet
text: A wild boar is tearing up the fields. The men are away at market.

success.text: The village eats pork for a month and calls you Little Tiger.

fail.text: It gores your thigh before fleeing.

choices.text: Lead it away into the hills

success.text: You lose it in the ravines.

fail.text: It is faster than it looks.

success.text: The millet is ruined. Winter will be thin.

title: The Dream of the Sword
text: You dream of standing on a mountain of swords. A voice asks: "What is a blade for?"

success.text: You wake with tears on your face and do not know why.
You wake with your fist clenched so hard it bleeds.
The voice sighs. You wake up hungry.

title: The Man Who Fishes Without a Hook
text: An old man sits by the lake with a straight needle on his line. "I am not fishing for fish," he says.

success.text: At nightfall he nods. "Patience. Good. Come back tomorrow, disciple."

fail.text: You fidget. He sighs. "Come back in ten years."

choices.text: Ask what he is fishing for

success.text: "A fool willing to ask." He taps your forehead and your qi stirs. Master Yun will teach you.

choices.text: Kick his bucket over and laugh

success.text: He does not move. You feel suddenly, deeply small.

title: The Stray
text: A half-starved dog follows you for three villages.

success.text: It guards your sleep ever after. One night its barking saves you from a thief.
An excellent accomplice.
It goes. You feel nothing, which is its own kind of answer.

title: Herbs on the Cliff
text: The apothecary pays well for cliff orchids. The cliff pays in broken necks.

success.text: A full basket, and thighs like iron.

fail.text: A handhold crumbles.

choices.text: Pick easy weeds and dye them purple

success.text: The apothecary pays. His patients may regret it.

title: Three Moves
text: A travelling swordsman watches you train and snorts. "Wrong. All wrong. Attack me. I will use three moves only."

success.text: You make him use a fourth. He leaves you a breathing method in thanks.

fail.text: You eat dirt three times. Each time teaches you something.

choices.text: Watch his feet, not his sword

success.text: You see it: the sword follows the step.

fail.text: You see nothing but sky.

title: The First Thread
text: Sitting in the cold, you feel a warm thread move below your navel for the first time.

success.text: It circles once and settles. Your first small circulation.
It breaks open a meridian. Painful, and worth it.

fail.text: It scatters like startled fish, leaving you coughing blood.

title: Fire in the Night
text: Bandits ride into your village with torches.

success.text: You kill a man for the first time. The village survives.

fail.text: A club takes you in the ribs. You wake among ashes.

choices.text: Hide the children in the well-house

success.text: Nine children live because of you.

choices.text: Show the bandits where your neighbour hid his grain, to spare your own house

success.text: They burn your house anyway, and laugh while doing it.

title: The Gate of Wudang
text: Mist rolls over a thousand steps. A Taoist hands each applicant a cup filled to the brim. "Climb. Spill nothing."

choices.text: Climb slowly, breathing with each step

success.text: At the top the cup is full and your mind is still. You are an outer disciple of Wudang.

fail.text: Halfway up your hands shake. Come back when you are calmer.

choices.text: Drink the water and refill the cup at the top spring

success.text: The Taoist bursts out laughing. "The Way is not rigid." You are in.

fail.text: "Out."

success.text: The mountain will not miss you.

title: The Temple Bell
text: Shaolin accepts lay disciples once a decade. The test: kneel in the courtyard for three days and nights.

success.text: On the third dawn a monk lifts you up. "The body is a boat. Yours floats."

fail.text: You faint on the second night. The monks leave you porridge and a blanket.

choices.text: Kneel, and sneak meat buns at night

success.text: Nobody notices. Buddha, presumably, does.

fail.text: A novice catches you mid-bite.

success.text: The bell tolls for someone else.

title: Plum Blossoms on the Cliff
text: Mount Hua tests applicants on a ledge no wider than a palm, with a wooden sword and a wind that wants you dead.

success.text: You cross with petals in your hair. The Mount Hua sect takes you in.

fail.text: You slip. A senior catches your collar, unimpressed.

success.text: You like your bones unbroken.

title: A Bowl and a Stick
text: A one-eyed beggar looks you over. "Poor enough. Sharp enough? The Beggars' Union has ears in every city under heaven."

success.text: You are given a cracked bowl, a stick, and ten thousand brothers.
"Yet," he agrees.

title: The Man in the Black Sedan
text: A pale man watches you train. "Talent is wasted on the righteous. The Heavenly Demon Cult asks no lineage. Only hunger."

success.text: You pass under a gate carved with screaming faces. There is no road back from here.
"We will ask again when the world has been unkind to you."

choices.text: Report him to the Alliance outpost

success.text: They miss him by an hour, but pay for the tip.

title: The Green Forest
text: You are surrounded on a forest road, but the bandit chief only laughs. "You have the look. Why bleed for coin when you can take it?"

success.text: You drink blood wine with thieves and wake up one of them.

choices.text: Refuse and fight your way out

success.text: You leave three of them groaning.

fail.text: They take your purse and your boots.

choices.text: Refuse politely and pay the toll

success.text: "A shame," says the chief, counting.

title: The Nightless Pavilion
text: You wake with a knife at your throat and a contract on your chest. "You passed," whispers a voice. "Most do not wake at all. We buy deaths. Will you sell them?"

success.text: You are given a mask, a number, and a first name to erase.
The knife withdraws. "Then forget this night."

fail.text: The knife leaves a scar to remember them by.

title: White Tiger Escort Agency
text: A notice on the wall: "Guards wanted. Pay on delivery. Funeral costs covered."

choices.text: Sign on as an escort guard

success.text: You are handed a banner and a spear.
A wage is a leash.

title: The Doctor's Errand
text: The town doctor, Old Hua, needs a pair of hands to grind herbs. "No pay. But you will learn which root kills and which cures."

success.text: Your fingers turn yellow with turmeric and your head fills with meridians.

choices.text: Steal his ginseng while he naps

success.text: It sells well.
Medicine is slow. You are in a hurry.

title: Bandits on the Mountain Road
text: Three men with rusted sabres block the pass. "Leave your purse, and keep your life."

success.text: They scatter after the first exchange.

fail.text: You escape, but not before a blade finds your shoulder.

success.text: Their curses fade behind you.

fail.text: A thrown club catches your back.

choices.text: Hand over your purse on your knees

success.text: They take it. One pats your head.

choices.text: Say you are the Green Forest chief's nephew

success.text: They escort you through the pass and apologise for the inconvenience.

title: The Cave Behind the Vines
text: Rain drives you into a cave. On the wall, half worn away, are carved figures in flowing stances.

choices.text: Study the carvings through the night

success.text: By dawn, your feet know what your mind cannot explain.

fail.text: You force the movements and your qi turns against you.

choices.text: Rest and leave at first light

success.text: You sleep soundly. Some doors are better left closed.

choices.text: Deface the wall. If you cannot learn it, no one will.

success.text: Petty, thorough work.

title: Beneath the Waterfall
text: The falls crash down like a wall of stone. Old masters are said to have tempered themselves here.

success.text: Your bones ache, then harden.

fail.text: The water throws you against the rocks.

success.text: The roar empties your mind. Qi gathers quietly.

title: The Wounded Swordsman
text: A man in torn white robes lies against a tree, one hand on a jewelled sword, breathing shallowly.

success.text: Before leaving, he presses two fingers to your brow. The world's qi becomes faintly visible.
He is too weak to stop you. The sword sells for a fortune.

fail.text: Even dying, his blade is faster than your eyes.

success.text: He looks at you until the end. In his robe is a token of the Namgung clan. They will want to know who did this.
The affairs of the martial world are not yours. Not yet.

title: The Tea House Rumour
text: A storyteller whispers of a manual hidden in the capital. A dice game rattles in the corner.

success.text: The dice love you tonight.

fail.text: You lose your coin and your temper.

success.text: Between the lies you catch a true principle of breath.

fail.text: It is only a story after all.

choices.text: Load the dice with a sliver of lead

success.text: Nobody sees. Nobody ever sees.

fail.text: Somebody sees.

title: The Serpent's Herb
text: A nine-leaf spirit herb glows on a ledge. Coiled around it sleeps a serpent as thick as your leg.

success.text: Its head falls. You eat the herb where you stand.

fail.text: Its fangs sink into your arm before you break free.

success.text: You pluck the herb and are gone before it stirs.

fail.text: A pebble shifts. The serpent strikes.

success.text: Your feet barely touch stone. The serpent never wakes.
Treasure is worthless to the dead.

title: The Heart Demon
text: Deep in meditation, a figure with your own face appears. "Why struggle? You were born ordinary. You will die ordinary."

success.text: "Then I will be ordinary, and walk on anyway." The figure bows and fades.

fail.text: Its words take root. You wake coughing blood.

success.text: You open your eyes. It will return another day.

title: The Arrogant Young Master
text: A silk-robed youth from a great clan blocks your way. "You looked at me. Kneel, or fight."

success.text: He lies in the dust. The crowd will remember your name.

fail.text: His guards carry you out of the square.

success.text: His qi stutters on every third breath. One palm is enough.
He spits and walks on. The crowd will remember that too.

choices.text: Kneel, then stab him in the foot and run

success.text: His scream follows you down three streets. You are laughing.

fail.text: His guards are faster.

title: The Magistrate's Tax
text: A village is being bled dry. The magistrate's men carry off the seed grain while he watches from a sedan chair.

success.text: They flee. The villagers hide you when the soldiers come.

fail.text: You are beaten in the square as a lesson to others.

choices.text: Rob the magistrate's vault at night and return the grain

success.text: By dawn every door has a sack on its step. No one knows who.

fail.text: A guard dog. Then guards.

success.text: He returns the grain himself, sweating, and begs you to mention his diligence at court.

choices.text: Offer the magistrate your services as an enforcer

success.text: The pay is good. The work is hitting farmers.
The road goes on. So do you.

title: The Widow's Debt
text: A moneylender's thugs are dragging a girl from a widow's house. "The debt is the debt."

success.text: The widow presses her forehead to the ground. You feel lighter than your purse.
They leave their teeth and the contract behind.

fail.text: There are more of them than you counted.

choices.text: Buy the debt yourself and collect it harder

success.text: The widow works your fields for ten years. You call it business.
The girl's screaming stops at the end of the lane.

title: The Fighting Stage
text: A red platform in the market square. "Ten taels to whoever stays standing against Iron Arm Guo!"

success.text: He goes over the ropes. The crowd roars.

fail.text: You are the one who goes over the ropes.

success.text: Guo swings at a man who is never where he was. He falls over on his own.

choices.text: Climb up with a fistful of sand

success.text: He claws at his eyes while you collect the prize. The crowd boos.

fail.text: Even blind he finds you.

success.text: He wins, as he always does.

fail.text: Today of all days, he loses.

title: The Inn With No Other Guests
text: The innkeeper smiles too much. The wine is free. The meat is unfamiliar.

success.text: Just a lonely innkeeper after all. You sleep well.

fail.text: You wake tied to a butcher's table and escape through the window, missing some skin.

success.text: Sleeping drug. You switch the cups and loot the cellar while he snores.

choices.text: Tip the table over and draw steel

success.text: In the cellar lie the bones of forty travellers. The county posts your name in thanks.

fail.text: The cook's cleaver is very fast.

success.text: The horse is better company anyway.

title: Mistaken for a Hero
text: A village crowds around you. "The Azure Sword! The hero who slew the Twin Wolves!" You have never heard of him.

success.text: Disappointed, they give you a bowl of rice anyway.
Roast pig, wine, and silk sheets. All you have to do is keep nodding.

title: The Hero Is Needed
text: The village elder bows. "Azure Sword, the Twin Wolves' cousins are riding here for revenge. Protect us."

success.text: You bleed for a lie and make it true. They carve your own name on the gate this time.

fail.text: You hold the gate until the militia arrives. A fraud, but not a coward.

choices.text: Slip out the back at midnight with the gift chest

success.text: You hear the screams from the next hill and walk faster.

title: The Real Azure Sword
text: A tall man in blue enters the tavern where you are signing autographs. He has heard of you. Or rather, of himself.

success.text: He laughs until he cries, then makes you pay for his drinks for a month.
The crowd throws vegetables at the most famous swordsman in the province. You will pay for this someday.

fail.text: He draws. The crowd sees at once which of you is real.

success.text: Out the window, over the wall, into legend of a different kind.

fail.text: He catches your collar mid-leap.

title: The Burning House
text: Flames eat a merchant's mansion. From one window, a child's cries. From another, the glint of a strongbox.

success.text: You come out black with smoke, a small heartbeat against your chest.

fail.text: The beam falls. You both live, barely.

success.text: Heavy with silver. The crying has stopped by the time you are out.

fail.text: The floor gives way. You get neither gold nor forgiveness.

success.text: The house is lost. The neighbours' homes are not.

title: Sixty Years of Qi
text: In a cave a dying old man grips your wrist. "Swear to kill the Ghost-Faced Judge, who betrayed me, and I will pour sixty years of cultivation into you."

success.text: His qi roars into you like a river in flood. His last breath is a smile.
Free power. Oaths are just air.

choices.text: "I will not swear what I may not keep."

success.text: He stares, then nods. "Honest. Take this instead." A small jade pill.

title: The Ghost-Faced Judge
text: You find him at last: an old man in a paper mask, feeding carp. "So he sent you. Did he tell you why I betrayed him?"

success.text: The oath is kept. The carp scatter.

fail.text: He disarms you gently and sends you home.

success.text: "He was selling children to the Blood Cult." He shows you the ledgers. You burn the oath with them.

title: The Overloaded Ferry
text: Mid-river, in a storm, the ferry is sinking. "Too heavy!" screams the boatman.

success.text: Your gold sinks. The boat rises.
Your arms burn, but everyone reaches shore.

fail.text: The boat capsizes near the bank. You haul out who you can.

success.text: The boat rises. No one meets your eyes for the rest of the crossing.

title: Small Hands
text: A filthy child bumps into you. Your purse is gone.

success.text: You catch a wrist as thin as a chopstick.

fail.text: Gone, like a rat into a wall.

success.text: Someone needed it more.

title: Small Hands, Caught
text: The child trembles. Behind a wall, a smaller sibling is coughing.

choices.text: Take back your purse and leave them a few coins

success.text: The child stares at the coins as if they might bite.

choices.text: Take back your purse and box the brat's ears

success.text: A lesson, of a kind.

choices.text: Take your purse, and the child's own coppers as a fine

success.text: Justice.

title: The Manual at Auction
text: An auction house offers a "genuine fragment of the Stone Turtle Scripture." Opening bid: 50 gold.

success.text: It is real. Your skin learns to turn a blade.
Half of tonight's other lots are forged. You say so loudly; grateful bidders tip you.

fail.text: You call the wrong item fake. The auctioneer has you thrown out.

success.text: You vanish with the scroll.

fail.text: The house guards are retired sect elders.

title: The Drunk in the Gutter
text: A reeking drunk in the gutter kicks away three ruffians without waking up.

success.text: He drinks for three days and, between hiccups, teaches you to fight like falling water.
A purse of silver and a jade gourd. He never stirs.

fail.text: His foot finds your jaw, still asleep.

success.text: Just a drunk.

title: The Poisoned Well
text: Half a town lies sick. Someone has fouled the well.

success.text: You trace it to an apothecary selling the "cure." The town hangs him and feasts you.

fail.text: You accuse the wrong man. He nearly hangs before the truth comes out.

success.text: By morning the fever breaks in forty houses.
They pay with their last coins and shaking hands.

choices.text: Leave before you get sick too

success.text: Sensible.

title: A Purse on the Road
text: A fat purse lies in the dust, embroidered with a merchant house's seal. Fifty gold, at least.

choices.text: Return it to the merchant house

success.text: The old merchant's eyes go wide. "An honest person! In this era?" He gives you ten gold and his friendship.
Heaven drops gold; who are you to refuse?

choices.text: Keep it, then claim the reward for "trying to find the thief"

success.text: The merchant thanks you warmly. You almost feel bad. Almost.

title: The Mob and the Healer
text: Torches. A crowd drags a herb-woman toward a pyre. "Witch! The fever came after she did!"

success.text: They know your name, and lower their torches.

fail.text: A stone opens your scalp, but they lose their nerve at the blood.

choices.text: Draw your sword and dare them

success.text: The mob breaks. She treats your cuts with shaking hands.

fail.text: Mobs do not duel. They trample. She escapes in the chaos.

success.text: Business is business. The fire is very bright.
You do not look back at the glow.

title: A Polite Challenge
text: A letter, in fine calligraphy: "I travel seeking the limits of my sword. At dawn, by the willow, if you would honour me."

success.text: He bows deeply in defeat and gifts you his insight.

fail.text: He bows deeply in victory and binds your wound himself.

choices.text: Ambush him on his way there

success.text: He dies surprised. His sword is very fine.
Your calligraphy is terrible. He frames it anyway.

title: The Hut in the Snow
text: Above the snow line, a hermit's hut. A sign: "Knock once. Then wait."

success.text: Three days in the snow. On the fourth the door opens. "You may stay the winter."

fail.text: On the second night you give up. The door never moved.

success.text: Empty. Dust on everything. A note on the table: "Too late by forty years. Or too impatient."
Some wisdom is not for sale at any price you can pay yet.

title: The Golden Toad Den
text: Dice, smoke, and the click of tiles. A man with gold teeth waves you to the high table.

success.text: Tonight the toad spits gold.

fail.text: You lose everything on the table.

choices.text: Borrow from the house and bet big

success.text: You triple it and walk out a legend of the tables.

fail.text: The man with gold teeth smiles. "You owe the Toad now."

success.text: The only winning move.

title: The Toad's Collectors
text: Four men with clubs. "The Toad sends regards. And interest."

success.text: They count it twice and leave.
They limp home. The Toad will send better next time.

fail.text: They break two of your fingers as a deposit.

choices.text: Point them to your sworn brother's house instead

success.text: "He will cover it," you say. He does, with his blood.
They take your coat, your boots, and your dignity.

title: The Toad Himself
text: The man with gold teeth sits in your room when you return. "I do not want your money anymore. I want a favour. A rival of mine needs to stop breathing."

success.text: A quiet knife in a quiet alley. The debt is cleared.
His den burns. A hundred debtors drink to your name.

fail.text: His bodyguards were behind the screen.

choices.text: Sell him your sect's patrol routes instead

success.text: He is delighted. Your seniors will wonder how the smugglers got so clever.

title: The Execution Ground
text: A swordsman kneels under the headsman's blade. The crowd whispers he was framed for refusing the governor's bribe.

success.text: You cut the ropes and ride out through arrows. A song is written by nightfall.

fail.text: You escape alone, with an arrow in you and his eyes on your back.

choices.text: Take the headsman's place under the hood

success.text: The blade comes down on the ropes. You are both gone before anyone understands.
The blade falls. The crowd goes home for lunch.
Everyone is looking at the blade.

title: The Price on Your Head
text: A woman with a crossbow and your portrait steps onto the road. "Nothing personal. Three hundred taels."

success.text: You leave her tied to a tree with her own rope.

fail.text: A bolt in the leg. You escape into the river.

choices.text: Pay her more than the bounty

success.text: "A pleasure." She tears up the portrait.

choices.text: Tell her your "partner" has a bigger bounty, and where he sleeps

success.text: She thanks you. You never had a partner; you just named someone you dislike.

title: The Checkpoint
text: Soldiers are checking every face against a wall of posters. Yours is third from the left.

success.text: He looks at you, at the poster, at the coins. "Never seen you."

choices.text: Go over the wall at night

success.text: Shadows are an old friend.

fail.text: A spear butt, a cell, and a week of beatings before you break out.

success.text: You walk through as an old washerwoman. The sergeant helps with your basket.

title: An Offer of Pardon
text: A tired magistrate slides a paper across the table. "The Mountain Butcher has killed thirty. Bring me his head, and your name is clean."

success.text: You return with a sack. The posters come down.

fail.text: He nearly adds you to his count.

choices.text: Bring him some other head. Who will check?

success.text: The magistrate does not check. A peddler's family will wonder why he never came home.
You have grown used to sleeping lightly.

title: The Map in the Sword Hilt
text: A rusted sword bought for scrap rattles. Inside the hilt: a map on oiled silk, marked "Where the Frost Sovereign sleeps."

success.text: You sew the map into your collar.
He pays without haggling, which means you sold too cheap.

choices.text: Sell ten copies to ten collectors, and keep the original

success.text: By the time they compare notes you are three provinces away.

title: The Tomb of the Frost Sovereign
text: The map ends at a glacier tomb. Inside stand a hundred frozen corpses of those who came before, and a pedestal with a sword of pale blue steel.

choices.text: Kneel before the sword and wait to be judged

success.text: The cold enters your heart, finds it steady, and yields. The blade is yours.

fail.text: The cold finds your doubts. You crawl out with frostbitten hands.

success.text: Your grip freezes to the hilt, but you do not let go. It accepts strength too.

fail.text: You join the statues for one long night before you tear free.

success.text: Rings, purses, a jade seal. The sword hums with contempt.

title: The Physician's Door
text: You are badly hurt. A lantern marks a physician's house.

success.text: Needles, poultices, and a week of sleep.

choices.text: Rest at the temple on charity

success.text: Thin gruel and kind monks.
You heal well on stolen ginseng.

title: A Quiet Season
text: No one is trying to kill you this year. It is almost unsettling.

success.text: You sleep late, eat well, and let your wounds knit.
Sweat and silence.
Honest coin for honest sweat.

title: The Man-Eater
text: A tiger has taken eleven people. The county offers fifty gold. The hunters who went up did not come down.

success.text: You come down the mountain wearing its skin.

fail.text: It leaves its signature across your chest.

title: The Murim Tournament
text: Banners over the capital: the Tournament of Rising Dragons. Every young sword under heaven is coming.

success.text: Your name is brushed onto the board.
Other people's dreams are a steady income.
You learn a great deal about your own limits.

title: The Semi-Final
text: You have reached the last four. Your opponent, the Namgung heir, visits your room the night before with a chest of gold. "Lose tomorrow."

success.text: You beat him in front of his whole clan.

fail.text: He did not need the bribe after all.

success.text: You fall convincingly in the ninth exchange.

choices.text: Take the gold and beat him anyway

success.text: He cannot exactly complain to the judges.

fail.text: Paid, and then beaten for real.

title: The Final
text: The arena falls silent. Across the sand stands the Little Sword Saint, undefeated.

success.text: When the dust settles, you are the one standing. Champion of the Rising Dragons.

fail.text: Second under heaven. The crowd chants your name anyway.

choices.text: Slip a numbing powder into his tea beforehand

success.text: His sword arm slows by a hair. It is enough. The trophy feels greasy.

title: The Exile From the Tang Clan
text: A thin man with stained fingertips shares your campfire. He was cast out of the Tang Clan for selling antidotes to the poor.

success.text: By dawn you know thirty poisons by smell, and their answers.

choices.text: Turn him in to the Tang Clan for the reward

success.text: They pay in gold, and warn you never to speak of it.
You sleep with one eye open.

title: The Alliance's Invitation
text: A letter sealed with the Murim Alliance's crest: "Your deeds are known. The Alliance would have you as a Guest Hero."

success.text: A jade token, a stipend, and a seat at councils that decide the fate of the martial world.
"A free blade serves justice better than a seated one." They respect it.

choices.text: Accept, and sell council gossip to the highest bidder

success.text: There is always a buyer.

title: The War of Righteous and Demonic
text: Beacon fires leap from peak to peak. The Heavenly Demon Cult has crossed the river in force. The whole murim must choose.

success.text: You tie a white band on your arm.
You tie a black band on your arm.
War is the best market there is.

title: The Battle of Broken Sword Ford
text: The Cult's vanguard is crossing. The Alliance line is wavering.

success.text: You take the enemy banner yourself. The line holds.

fail.text: You are carried from the water half dead. The line holds anyway.

success.text: Less glory. More people alive.
You rise when it is over and claim a kill or two.

title: The Burning of Clear Water Sect
text: Your column takes a small orthodox sect by surprise. The disciples are mostly children. Orders: no survivors.

success.text: The mountain burns for three days.

choices.text: Let the children flee through the back valley

success.text: "No one here," you report.

fail.text: An officer sees. You kill him to keep the secret.

choices.text: Loot the treasury while the others do the killing

success.text: Clean hands, full pockets. In a manner of speaking.

title: Swords for Sale
text: Both armies need steel. You know a smith with a warehouse full.

success.text: Fair price, fair cause.
Gold is gold. The dead do not ask who forged the blade.
Swords snap on both sides of the river. You are long gone.

title: The Road of Refugees
text: Thousands on the road with bundles and hollow eyes. A mother offers you her baby. "Take her somewhere there is food."

success.text: Three weeks of walking backwards with a drawn sword. All of them arrive.

fail.text: You lose some to the night. Never the baby.

success.text: It is not enough. It is something.

choices.text: Sell places on a "safe route" you invented

success.text: They pay everything they have and follow your map into the hills.
You keep your eyes on the horizon.

title: The Blade Pointing Inward
text: The Alliance sends the signal. It is time to open the Cult's fortress gate from within.

success.text: The Alliance pours in. Your name is cleared before ten thousand witnesses.

fail.text: You open it, and take a spear for it.

choices.text: Betray the Alliance instead. It was a double game all along.

success.text: The Alliance's best walk into a slaughter.

title: The Last Battle
text: The two armies meet on the Plain of Ten Thousand Graves. Whoever wins today owns the next hundred years.

choices.text: Fight for the Alliance and seek out the Cult's champion

success.text: You cut him down before both armies. The Cult breaks. They will sing of this until the mountains wear away.

fail.text: You fall. But the champion is wounded, and the Alliance prevails by a thread.

choices.text: Fight for the Cult and seek out the Alliance Leader

success.text: His white banner falls. The age of the righteous ends by your hand.

fail.text: He breaks your blade and your army. You escape in the rout.

choices.text: Watch from a hilltop and rob the dead afterwards

success.text: So many fine swords with no further use for their owners.

choices.text: Tend the wounded of both sides

success.text: Men in white bands and black bands lie side by side in your tent, too tired to hate.

title: The White Banner
text: The old Alliance Leader lays down his seal. Every sect looks to you.

success.text: You raise the white banner. For once, the murim is at peace.
"Heroes should not be rulers." You walk out, and are loved more for it.

choices.text: Accept, and begin selling Alliance posts

success.text: Peace is expensive. Someone should profit.

title: The Price of a Name
text: A young swordsman bows. "Defeating you would make my name. Please."

success.text: He leaves bruised and inspired.

fail.text: An upset. He is gracious; the gossips are not.

success.text: He will discover it someday, and understand.

choices.text: Have him beaten by hired thugs before the duel

success.text: He never arrives.

title: The Tale Grows
text: A storyteller is describing how you slew forty bandits with a chopstick. It was six, with a sword.

success.text: "Six? With a sword? Boo!" The crowd prefers his version.
By next year it will be four hundred.

choices.text: Pay him to add a dragon

success.text: An investment.

title: The Banquet Trap
text: A lord invites you to a banquet "in honour of your deeds". The servers move like killers.

success.text: You fight your way out through the main course.

fail.text: Poison in the third cup.

success.text: You swap cups with the host and bid him good health.
Fame is a target painted on the back.

title: Your Impostor
text: Someone is travelling the south, using your name to eat free and charm rich widows.

success.text: A scrawny fraud. You make him apologise to every village.
You remember being hungry too.

choices.text: Find him and take a cut

success.text: Your name works twice as hard now.

title: The Hero Is Tired
text: You are wounded and exhausted. A village elder kneels in the road. "Hero. Raiders, tonight. There is no one else."

success.text: You fight on your knees by the end. The village lives.

fail.text: You buy them time to flee to the hills. It costs you.

choices.text: Teach them to fight for themselves

success.text: Pitchforks, pits, and courage. They win their own battle.

fail.text: Farmers are not soldiers. You fill the gap yourself.

choices.text: Tell him you are someone else

success.text: He apologises for bothering you.

title: "Slay the Demon!"
text: Five young heroes block the road, swords trembling. "Villain! Today heaven's justice is done!"

success.text: Heaven's justice is running late.

fail.text: One of them is better than he looks.

choices.text: Disarm them and send them home

success.text: "Train ten more years." They will tell this story with shame, then with awe.

fail.text: Mercy is harder than murder.

success.text: They do not dare strike. That is its own answer.

title: The Town Kneels
text: You enter a town, and the streets empty. The headman crawls out with a tray of silver. "Please. Take it and spare us."

success.text: It is good to be feared.
They will be confused for years.
A reliable income.

title: Moths to a Black Flame
text: Killers, outcasts and madmen begin to gather around you, calling you Lord.

choices.text: Forge them into a sect of your own

success.text: The Black Sky Sect is born. The Alliance holds an emergency council.
You need no dogs.

choices.text: Use them up as bait and shields

success.text: They die adoring you.

title: The Orphan You Made
text: A youth with burning eyes: "You killed my father at Three Pines. I have trained for this day for eleven years."

success.text: Like father, like child.
The blade goes in deep. The youth stares at the blood, drops the sword, and flees.
You truly do not remember. That is the worst thing you could have said.

title: The Bell at Dusk
text: A temple bell, and an abbot who looks at you without fear. "Lay down the butcher's knife, and become a Buddha where you stand."

success.text: You shave your head. The names of your dead become your sutra.
The bell rings on behind you.
So much for Buddhas.

title: The Alliance Marches on You
text: A thousand swords of the righteous sects surround your lair. "Come out and face judgment!"

success.text: By dusk the slope is carpeted in white robes. The murim will not sleep soundly for a generation.

fail.text: You escape through the back tunnels, alone, your power broken.

success.text: Black qi rolls down the mountain like a tide. Those who can still run, run.

choices.text: Escape in disguise, leaving your followers to die

success.text: Their last stand buys you two days.
They cripple your cultivation and chain you beneath a mountain. In the dark, you finally have time to think.

title: No Service
text: The tavern keeper recognises you. "Not you. Out. I heard what you did."

success.text: The door slams.
He takes the money and spits in your soup. You eat it anyway.

choices.text: Claim to be your own twin brother

success.text: "People confuse us all the time. Terrible fellow." He half believes it.

title: The Ballad of the Rat
text: Children in the street are singing a rhyme about a certain coward and cheat. It has your name in it, and nine verses.

success.text: They scatter, singing louder. A tenth verse is composed about this.
It is catchy, to be fair.

choices.text: Pay a poet to write a counter-ballad

success.text: It is so bad that people sing it ironically.

title: Someone Knows
text: A letter under your door: "I know what you did. Fifty gold, under the bridge, or everyone knows."

success.text: Until the next letter.

choices.text: Wait under the bridge with a club

success.text: The blackmailer is a very surprised clerk.

choices.text: Publish it yourself. What is one more?

success.text: The town shrugs. Your reputation had nowhere left to fall.

title: The Guild of Shameless Men
text: A greasy man bows. "Senior! Your work is admired. The Guild of Shameless Men would be honoured: cheats, frauds, fake monks, the finest scum under heaven."

success.text: The secret handshake involves picking each other's pockets.
"A lone wolf. We respect that. We also took your purse."

choices.text: Join, then sell the membership list to the magistrate

success.text: Even they are impressed.

title: The Invincible Tiger-Crane Academy
text: You could open a martial school. You would not need to teach anything real. Parents pay monthly.

success.text: Forty students practise "the Stance of Standing Still" while you count fees.
It earns less. A few students actually improve. So, strangely, do you.
Too much paperwork.

title: A Real Master Visits
text: A genuine master walks into your academy. "I hear you teach the Tiger-Crane. Show me."

success.text: You win. Years of dodging consequences have made you fast.

fail.text: Your students watch their master fly through a wall.

choices.text: "The true art is too deadly to demonstrate."

success.text: Half the students believe you. The other half demand refunds.

choices.text: Pay a student to fight in your place

success.text: The student wins. The student opens a rival school.

title: The Guild's Grand Scheme
text: The Guild plans its masterpiece: selling a "Dragon Vein Treasure Map" to five great clans at once.

success.text: Five clans dig up the same empty hill and blame each other. You retire three provinces away.
Betraying the betrayers. The clans reward you; the Guild expels you with honours.

title: The One You Wronged
text: A beggar by the road: someone you cheated, long ago, ruined by it. They do not recognise you.

success.text: You leave a hundred gold and no name. It does not erase anything. It is still worth doing.
They stare. Then they hit you with the begging bowl until it breaks. You let them.
They call a blessing after you, for the coin you did not give.

title: Crowned
text: At the annual gathering of the underworld's lowest, they place a crown of chicken bones on your head. "The Rat King! Ten thousand years!"

success.text: You give a speech. It is mostly lies. They weep.
Even you have limits, apparently. News to everyone.

title: Old Wounds
text: Rain is coming; your scars told you an hour ago. The body keeps accounts.

success.text: Slower than once. Still moving.

choices.text: Soak in hot springs and medicine

success.text: An old warrior's small luxuries.
You watch the rain and name each scar.

title: Ink and Memory
text: A lifetime of swordplay sits in your hands and nowhere else. If you die, it dies.

success.text: Three volumes. Future generations will bow to your portrait.

choices.text: Write it with deliberate errors, so no one surpasses you

success.text: A trap for the unborn.

choices.text: Burn your notes. Let them find their own way.

success.text: The sword cannot be written anyway.

title: The Youth at the Gate
text: A fierce youth kneels at your gate for three days. "Fight me. I need to know how far I have to go."

success.text: You win, barely. You show the youth exactly where the gap is.

fail.text: The youth wins, and weeps, because the mountain turned out to be climbable.

success.text: "Put the sword down and pick up the broom. We start tomorrow."

choices.text: Have your servants chase the brat off

success.text: Legends should not answer doors.

title: The Last Gift
text: Your time is short. You could pour your lifetime of qi into your disciple. It would kill you. It would make them great.

success.text: You sit behind your disciple, palms on their back, and empty yourself like a cup. Your last sight is their tears.
You live, diminished. They rise.
The disciple bows, and hides the disappointment well.

title: An Old Enemy, Older
text: A bent old man waits on your doorstep with a sword and a wine jar. You broke his arm forty years ago.

success.text: You talk until the jar is empty. Neither of you remembers what the fight was about.
He dies smiling. "Finally." You bury him yourself.

fail.text: He wins at last, and helps you up. "Now we are even."

success.text: Old grudges, old methods.

title: The Mountain Calls
text: You find a hut above the clouds. Silence. A spring. No one who knows your name.

success.text: You sweep leaves, and the years, from the doorstep.
The murim is not done with you.

choices.text: Stay, and advertise yourself as a mysterious sage for hire

success.text: "The Sage of Cloud Peak answers three questions for thirty gold."

title: The Mountain of Swords, Again
text: The dream returns after a lifetime. The same voice: "What is a blade for?"

success.text: "And did you?" You look back down your life, and can answer.
"And was it enough?" The swords fall silent, waiting.
"Good," says the voice, almost fondly. "Keep walking."

title: Lanterns, Fifty Years On
text: The lantern festival. You have seen fifty of them. Children run past with paper tigers.

choices.text: Buy lanterns for the street children

success.text: A hundred small lights float up, each carrying a wish you paid for.

choices.text: Sit by the river and remember

success.text: Faces rise with the lanterns. Not all of them are angry.

choices.text: Cut purses in the crowd, for old times' sake

success.text: Still got it.

title: The Sword Saint
text: The Sword Saint, undefeated for sixty years, sends a single plum blossom. An invitation.

success.text: One stroke each. His sleeve falls, cut. He laughs like a boy. "At last!" The murim has a new peak.

fail.text: One stroke each. You lose a lock of hair and gain a lifetime of insight.

choices.text: Ask to be taught rather than tested

success.text: "No one has asked in forty years. They all want to beat me." He pours tea.

choices.text: Send an assassin's needle with your reply

success.text: He catches it between two fingers and sends back a single word: "Shameful." The whole murim reads it.

title: The Ruins Open
text: Once in a century, the mist over the Ten Thousand Sword Ruins lifts. Masters from every faction rush in.

success.text: You follow a cold wind to a sealed chamber.

fail.text: A collapsing corridor nearly ends you at the threshold.

success.text: Let others do the dying. You take their finds at the exit.
Half of those who enter never return.

title: The Sealed Chamber
text: A skeleton sits in meditation, a jade slip in its lap. Three other masters arrive at the same moment.

success.text: The slip holds a lost art of the ancients.

fail.text: You leave with your life and little else.

choices.text: Propose that all four share it

success.text: Suspicion, then a shaky truce, then four masters sitting around a skeleton, copying notes.

fail.text: They take that as weakness.

success.text: The floor opens under the other three. A second, hidden slip falls from the skeleton's sleeve into your hands.

fail.text: Nothing happens. The others take the slip while your head is down.

title: The Ranking of Heaven and Earth
text: The Hall of Records publishes its list of the ten greatest martial artists alive. Your name is on it.

success.text: Challengers will come. Let them.
They revise it. You are third under heaven.

fail.text: They do not. People snicker.

choices.text: Bribe the Hall for first place

success.text: First under heaven, by purchase. Everyone knows. Everyone bows anyway.

title: The Door in the Sky
text: At the peak of the Profound realm, the sky opens above you like an eye. Beyond it: something vast. The murim has a word for this. Ascension.

success.text: You rise, and the mountains grow small, and then the world. What you become, no tale can follow.

choices.text: Stay. There is still work here.

success.text: The door closes without resentment. It will open again when you ask.
